title: Cloudflare-fronted public uploads silently fail at >100 MB body
description: Cloudflare free plan caps proxied request bodies at 100 MB. Bigger uploads return Cloudflare-generated 413 HTML before the request reaches uvicorn — backend access logs show no entry for the failed POSTs. Frontend's 200 MB cap mismatched the real limit, so users picked 150-200 MB FLACs and saw '失敗 10%' with no useful message. Verified: curl POSTing a 150 MB body to /api/process/upload returns 413 from CF after ~1.5 MB upload bytes. User repro: Africa.flac at 183 MB. Mobile worked because that file was under 100 MB. Fix: cap to 100 MB on frontend public mode + clear FLAC→MP3 conversion hint in the alert.
close_reason: Deployed via 7c5a4d8. Cloudflare free plan caps body at 100 MB — confirmed via curl test (150 MB POST returns 413 from CF edge after ~1.5 MB upload). Frontend now caps to 100 MB on _isPublicMode with a clear FLAC→MP3 conversion hint; personal/beta mode keeps 200 MB. Backend MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES stays at 200 MB as secondary guard.

title: Cover extraction: R2 path uploads with key='pending', never renamed to result_hash
description: On VPS with LIVECHORD_USE_R2=1, _extract_cover(audio_path, 'pending') uploads to R2 with key 'pending'. The follow-up 'pending.jpg → {result_hash}.jpg' rename only handles local disk (Path.rename). R2 path leaves the cover at key 'pending' and /api/process/cover/<result_hash> returns 404. Affects every cover-having upload on https://livechord.org. Fix: extract bytes synchronously, upload after result_hash known.
close_reason: Deployed via 6464835. Cover: refactored _extract_cover into _read_cover_bytes (pure read) + _persist_cover (writes after result_hash known) so R2 path no longer strands covers under key 'pending'. Existing R2 covers under 'pending' are unrecoverable but new uploads write to the correct key. Auto-split: added halved-downbeats fallback in chord_splitter — when raw bpb ∈ [1.7, 2.3] and 2*bpb ∈ [3,5], use every other downbeat. Air Supply 'Out Of Nothing At All' (hash e3ee0776cdb0) now splits 89 → 118 chords with reason 'ok-halved-downbeats'; player shows bar-sized cards (G 0:00, G 0:03, Em7 0:07, Em7 0:10) instead of the previous 7-second mega-cards. 25/25 chord_splitter tests pass.

title: beat_refiner downbeat over-density: 4/4 misread as 2/4 breaks player
description: Backfill v2 over-densified downbeats on subset of 7,967 applied songs (model thinks 4/4 is 2/4, halves bar duration). chord_splitter trusts downbeats blindly, makes cards too short. player auto_split forces 4 dots evenly across short cards = 2x/4x apparent dot speed. Also player auto_split bypasses manual BPM override (regression from chord_splitter commit). Fix: (1) phase1_refine gate rejects when beats_per_bar drops to ~2 from ~4, (2) chord_splitter sanity check on bar/bpm consistency, (3) player auto_split honors bpmMult override, (4) selective .bak restore for affected songs (preserve ~6.5-7.5k legit improvements). Examples: Abyss Levoire Combat 2 (beats_per_bar 4->2), user-reported.
close_reason: 3-layer fix shipped (commit 4db2660): phase1_refine bpb gate, chord_splitter sanity check, player auto_split honors override + sanity. Selective restore (commit pending) reverted 2,588 of 7,967 over-densified songs. Net: 5,379 legit refinements kept.

title: Guitar RH visual ≠ MIDI audio (architectural)
description: The guitar/ukulele _drawRhWaterfall in string-instrument.js calls _generateRhEvents(chords, bpm) — a CLIENT-SIDE arpeggio pattern generator that's completely independent from accData.right_hand (the backend-generated audio events). On piano tab the visual + audio both consume accData; on guitar/uke tabs the visual diverges. User sees 'string A (p) at beat 2-3, but MIDI plays it on beat 1' — visible specifically when switching from piano to guitar mid-playback. Fix options: (A) make _generateRhEvents output also feed audio synth (need to map ev.strings → MIDI pitches via diagram); (B) make _drawRhWaterfall consume accData.right_hand and render piano-pitch events on guitar strings (lossy mapping but visual = audio); (C) make the BACKEND emit guitar-style event types (strum/pick) when style=Guitar and have synth handle them. Punt for now; needs design discussion.
notes:
SESSION HANDOFF — branch: feature/ai-accompaniment-styles, last commit b5244f8.

## Reproduction
1. Open any song with Guitar tab as default (or switch mid-playback piano→guitar).
2. Use AI Accompaniment with style=PopBallad or any arpeggio-mode style.
3. Watch waterfall: bass thumb (p) appears at beat ~2.5 visually
4. Listen: bass note plays correctly on beat 1.
5. Verified ✅ on http://192.168.50.6:8800/player?path=...Cupid... (key D, BPM 120)

## Critical files (read before touching)
- [frontend/js/string-instrument.js:336-398](frontend/js/string-instrument.js#L336) — _generateRhEvents arpeggio path
- [frontend/js/string-instrument.js:400-430](frontend/js/string-instrument.js#L400) — _drawRhWaterfall (calls _generateRhEvents)
- [frontend/js/arpeggio-patterns.js](frontend/js/arpeggio-patterns.js) — pima/pimami/pami/pima_chord/travis/folk/pop_ballad pattern definitions
- [frontend/js/player.js:6481](frontend/js/player.js#L6481) — scheduleNotes audio scheduler (consumes accData.right_hand)
- [frontend/js/player.js:_resolveRhEvents](frontend/js/player.js) — RH event resolver, respects rhContentMode
- [backend/ai/accompaniment_generator.py _build_right_hand](backend/ai/accompaniment_generator.py) — backend RH generator (engine v5 period-tile)

## Why this matters
After my engine v5 period-tile fix (commit 95e62a3), audio events tile at fixed beat-period from chord.time → bar-aware. Guitar visual still uses cycleDur from chord.time. For 4-beat chords starting on bar boundary they coincide; for 2-beat chords or chords on offbeats they diverge.

## Three fix options (choose one in next session)

**Option A — visual→audio**: map _generateRhEvents events to MIDI pitches via the chord diagram (strings[s].fret + open-string MIDI). Replace audio-side accData.right_hand consumption when on guitar/uke tab with the local generator output. Pros: visual always wins. Cons: loses backend's velocity humanization, melody-gap awareness.

**Option B — audio→visual**: _drawRhWaterfall consumes accData.right_hand. Map each piano-pitch event to nearest guitar string (lossy — multiple pitches → same string collide). Lose the strum/pick semantics. Pros: minimal code change. Cons: visual doesn't look like a guitar anymore.

**Option C — backend extension**: STYLE_CONFIG gets style_family field. When 'string', _build_right_hand emits {type, strings, finger, time, dur} events. Synth playback path unchanged (still uses pitch). Add a string→pitch resolver on synth side. Pros: cleanest, audio + visual share source. Cons: backend cache schema bump (engine v5→v6), most code changed.

**Recommended: C** — biggest investment, lowest long-term tech debt. Visual + audio share one truth.

## Acceptance criteria
- Guitar visual + MIDI audio arpeggio events fire at IDENTICAL absolute times for any chord+style combination.
- Switching tab mid-playback (piano→guitar) doesn't introduce a phase offset.
- Existing piano tab behavior unchanged.
- Existing accordion/arranger tabs unchanged (they consume accData directly via the keyboard waterfall, no _generateRhEvents).

## Out of scope for this issue
- Pattern-set design (pima/folk/etc) — keep as-is, just unify the rendering source.
- Velocity / humanization — engine v5 already handles this on audio side.
- LH side — no divergence reported.

## How to confirm before merging
- Playwright: open Cupid.flac, AI Acc style=Auto, switch to guitar, advance to second beat of measure 2, getBoundingClientRect of the bottom-most strum bar should match floor(audio.currentTime * pxPerSec) within 1px.

value: Cloudflare free plan request body limit: 100 MB. Pro/free both 100 MB; Business 200 MB; Enterprise 500 MB. Applies to bodies via Cloudflare Tunnel too — body is buffered/checked at CF edge BEFORE forwarding through the tunnel. A 413 from CF returns an HTML error page, not JSON, so client fetch sees an empty res.statusText and surfaces an empty error message. Workaround for users: convert FLAC to MP3 320 kbps (~12 MB / 5 min) or get a Cloudflare paid plan.

Engine v7 (deployed 2026-05-06 to livechord.org via feature/beta-productization, fef9279). String idiom routes by STYLE NAME not piano rh_mode — STRING_IDIOM_BY_STYLE in accompaniment_generator.py. arpeggio: Arpeggio/Alberti/1+3/PopBallad/RockBallad/RnBNeoSoul. offbeat: Reggae/BossaNova/JazzCharleston/JazzWaltz. strum: everything else. STRING_OPEN_MIDI per instrument (guitar [40,45,50,55,59,64], ukulele reentrant [55,48,52,57]). Cache filename: {h}_{style}_{level}_{section}_{instrument}_v7.json — engine version is the invalidation knob. Bumping ACC_ENGINE_VERSION orphans old guitar/uke caches; lazy regen on next playback. Frontend gotcha: encodeURIComponent on style param is REQUIRED (1+3 has literal +, otherwise decodes to space and falls through STYLE_DICT). Reason: rh_mode names piano gap-fill behavior, not guitar idiom — naive routing put 'Arpeggio' into strum bucket via fill_only fallback.

R2 cover bug pattern: any code path that writes data to R2/S3 under a placeholder key with intent to 'rename later' is broken — object stores have no rename, only put. Pattern: extract bytes synchronously (pure read), persist AFTER the canonical key is known. Bit us once with _extract_cover('pending') in process_queue; fixed by splitting into _read_cover_bytes + _persist_cover and reordering the call sites.

Don't read livechord_guest_acked from layout/CTA logic on the public homepage. The flag is sticky in localStorage and survives across browser sessions, so any CTA branch that special-cases on it can become unreachable for returning users — they cannot reach /login from the homepage at all. Pattern that works: localStorage stores the ack as historical state, but interactive logic (CTA routing, layout selection) must always treat 'no token' as logged-out. The actual guest-upload affordance is a /login -> /?upload=1 redirect that frontend/js/app.js consumes via a URLSearchParams check on page load — guests reach the upload modal in one click without the homepage code ever caring whether the flag is set. Bit us once: 'continue as guest -> / -> CTA opens modal forever, user cannot log in'. Fix shipped on commit chain ending at the app.js v=97 / i18n.js v=34 cache-bust.

Cache-bust discipline reminder: bumping CSS file content is not enough — also bump the ?v= query string in EVERY HTML file referencing it. Bit us once with player.css edit deploying but accordion overlap appearing unfixed in QA because v=115 was still in player.html. Same applies to JS. Lesson: when editing a CSS or JS file, immediately bump every ?v= reference to it via 'grep -l <filename>?v= frontend/*.html | xargs sed -i'.

UI label drift pattern: when a user-facing label describes 'what's playing', drive it from the actual event/data stream, NOT from a user picker that's supposed to govern that stream. Picker state can stale-drift relative to what the audio/visual is actually doing (cached events, async reload race, picker becomes decorative after a refactor). Bit us twice on string-instrument.js _updateHints — first the rhInfo label read getStrumStyle() (a v5-era picker) while accData was the v6 ground truth; then the same label ignored rhContentMode while showing melody-mapped strings. Fix pattern: _inferAccIdiom(accData) infers idiom from event shape (strum_id/finger letters); _updateHints reads rhContentMode FIRST (rhMode='mel'->'RH melody', rhMode='both'->'RH acc+melody', else inferred). General lesson: UI labels should observe the live data, not the user's most recent picker click — if those disagree, the label is the canary.

V:\ deploy-sync gap pattern (recurring). Local commits' worth of fixes don't always propagate to V:\frontend if the only sync mechanism is manual cp during the original work session. Bit us TWICE this branch: (1) commit aa532f1 added position:relative on .acc-left-panel locally, V:\ stayed without it for ~24h until QA caught the accordion-overlap bug; (2) commits 557ffd3 + 9b0a9d6 + d8e4a6a fixed chord-render.js fret-jump label position locally, V:\ stayed with old body for ~3 days until QA caught the '1格 Fm7 與指法重疊' bug. Both fixes existed in git but the deployed code on NUC didn't have them. Detection: 'diff -q frontend/css/<f> /v/frontend/css/<f>' across the touched files at branch end; OR 'git log --all --pretty=format:%H -- frontend/<f>' vs file mtime on V:\ to spot files where V:\ hasn't been refreshed since the last code edit. Mitigation: at end of every work session, run a one-shot script that diff -q's every modified frontend file vs V:\ and warns on mismatch. Cache-bust ?v= alone doesn't help because V:\ AND local both need to bump in lockstep — the cache-bust value changes but the V:\ FILE CONTENT was never updated. Lesson: file-sync to V:\ is part of the COMMIT, not part of QA — always do cp before git commit, and have CI/preflight check (diff -q) as backstop.
